blocks.title: Pollutants
blocks.text: Pollutants are substances (gases, liquids and solids) that are harmful to the environment. Air pollutants are classified as primary, substances directly produced or emitted, such as ash from a volcanic eruption or carbon monoxide from a motor vehicle exhaust, and secondary, formed by chemical reactions of primary pollutants.

The most important pollutants are: oxides of carbon (CO and CO2); oxides of nitrogen (NO and NO2, collectively NOx); oxides of sulfur (SO2 and SO3, collectively SOx); hydrocarbons (methane, ethane); low-altitude ozone; chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs); polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs); persistent organic pollutants (POPs); volatile organic compounds (VOCs); particulate matter (PM); and heavy metals (Pb, Hg and Cd). Each is described in 14.4.

blocks.prompt: Mention the important air pollutants, and say which of ozone and sulfur dioxide is a secondary pollutant (Quick Check 14.1a; MCQ XI).
blocks.explanation: CO and CO2, NOx, SOx, hydrocarbons, low-altitude ozone, CFCs, PAHs, POPs, VOCs, particulate matter and the heavy metals lead, mercury and cadmium. Sulfur dioxide is primary, emitted directly from burning coal and oil; ground-level ozone is secondary, made in the air from NOx and VOCs in sunlight.

items: Pollutants harm the environment; primary = emitted directly, secondary = formed from primary pollutants. Eleven classes: COx, NOx, SOx, hydrocarbons, low-altitude O3, CFCs, PAHs, POPs, VOCs, PM, heavy metals.
